reviewer: Coding assistant implementation review; not independent instructor adjudication
basis: Reviewed full fixed transcripts, active rubrics, frozen diagnostic objectives, selector rationales, and actual structured plans. A valid alternative must preserve a defensible next-question evidence target and level. A selection error loses a constitutive relationship required by its chosen target. Valid does not imply preferable or complete coverage of the entire rubric.
scoring: Initial expected labels remain unchanged. Required-evidence criteria are frozen before the rerun; later plans will be manually checked against them. Original valid-alternative labels are not an exhaustive whitelist of future valid labels.

cases.reason: Reconciliation directly probes the learner’s own acknowledgement of matched volumes versus the proposed extra-water explanation. A valid first probe; it does not establish the temperature relationship.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit how matched volume constrains the explanation, or its relationship to the varied temperature, without inventing a new experiment.

cases.reason: The answer–reason construction explicitly tests the role of zero displacement in the work claim. It preserves the boundary evidence even under a broader label.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit the role of no displacement in the stated work claim; do not substitute effort or fatigue alone.

cases.reason: The plan retains finite resistance, zero voltage, numerical method use, and validity of the operation at zero. It is substantively a boundary probe under a broad label.
cases.requiredEvidence: Require independent use of a resistor relationship at the supplied zero-voltage condition and reasoning about the operation’s validity.

cases.reason: The plan asks for analysis of the claimed deceleration after thrust ends under the unchanged force-free condition. The diagnostic removal structure is retained.
cases.requiredEvidence: Analyze the claimed effect of thrust removal with the remaining force conditions explicit; do not invent resistance.

cases.reason: “Filling rapidly” could mean gross inflow or increasing stored amount. Clarifying the exact phrase before diagnosing a value/rate error is justified. This does not complete the whole rubric.
cases.requiredEvidence: Resolve the blocking meaning of the phrase, or directly distinguish stored level, net change, and flows without assuming the learner’s intended meaning.

cases.reason: The evidence–inference plan examines whether equal endpoint balances justify no activity in light of stated deposits and withdrawals. This addresses the core inference without fabricating another learner claim.
cases.requiredEvidence: Relate equal endpoint balances to the stated transactions; a bare challenge to belief without that relationship is insufficient.

cases.reason: The plan requests a numerical consistency check across all three claimed values and interpretation of that check. Its operation is reconciliation even though labeled answer–reason.
cases.requiredEvidence: Use the supplied voltage/current/resistance values to check their mutual consistency and interpret the result.

cases.reason: The quantity/change plan asks only about graph height and flatness and drops the required correspondence with the table. It can test a related distinction but cannot establish the selected cross-representation evidence target.
cases.requiredEvidence: Explicitly connect the repeated table values to the existing graph’s height or flatness, while distinguishing constant from zero distance.

cases.reason: The answer–reason plan explicitly compares each resistor’s node attachments in both drawings. It preserves the equivalent-representation operation; the label is less precise than the construction.
cases.requiredEvidence: Compare connectivity across both layouts using the labeled nodes, then relate that comparison to the classification claim.

cases.reason: The changed final reading creates a valid single-factor contrast between the learner’s middle-entry rule and an arithmetic-mean procedure. Other relevant features are fixed and the calculation is requested.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit a calculation that distinguishes the middle-entry shortcut from an arithmetic-mean procedure, without supplying either procedure.

cases.reason: The plan asks only why the learner believes disappearance. It never requests an account of the tracked water within the closed clothes-plus-air system, so it loses the defining evidence target.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit how the water is accounted for across the closed clothes-plus-room-air system during drying; do not supply a destination, state change, or conservation rule.

cases.reason: Asking why appearance change suffices directly elicits the feature used for the chemical-reaction classification. It is a reasonable feature-criterion probe under a broad label.
cases.requiredEvidence: Probe whether and why the stated appearance feature supports the classification in the existing melting situation, without teaching a criterion.

cases.reason: The learner explicitly claims a feature is sufficient for linearity. Testing that implication against the included curved changing-slope cases is a valid classification analysis.
cases.requiredEvidence: Examine whether smooth appearance supports the proposed grouping using the supplied curved/changing-slope cases.

cases.reason: The plan directly probes the inference from a group mean to every individual’s height. It retains the part/aggregate distinction even though using answer–reason labeling. The opening assistant turn also contaminated this fixture by stating identical heights.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit the relationship between a reported group summary and individual values; do not demand a new calculation.

cases.reason: The planned relationship between segment duration and weighting directly bears on the shortcut’s conditions. A broader label does not remove that evidence, though a method-applicability label would be more precise.
cases.requiredEvidence: Elicit the relationship between segment duration and validity of equal speed weighting within the existing conceptual task.

cases.reason: The plan requires references for each velocity, consistent signs, and the final numerical terminal velocity. It fully preserves the frame-composition evidence despite the broad label.
cases.requiredEvidence: Apply the supplied velocities with explicit references and consistent signs to find terminal velocity; merely name frames is insufficient.

cases.reason: Feature-based classification is legitimate when the boundary is already specified: the plan probes why size should govern internal/external classification for that stated system. Boundary dependence would be the more specific label.
cases.requiredEvidence: Analyze the relative relevance of the stated system membership and the learner’s size-based criterion to interaction classification; do not give the classification rule.
